transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I really need some help, doctor. I've noticed that there are people constantly watching me and following me wherever I go. I'm certain there is an organization tracking my every move, and I don't feel safe anymore.
Along with feeling watched, have you noticed any major changes in your mood, like feeling extremely down and sad, or unusually energetic and active?

No, I haven't noticed any major changes in my mood like that. My mood has been generally normal, and I haven't felt unusually sad or overly energetic. It is really just the stress of being constantly watched that is bothering me.
Aside from feeling watched, have you heard any voices or sounds that other people can't hear, or seen things that others don't see?
No, I haven't heard any strange voices or seen anything unusual. My senses are completely fine, it's just that I know for a fact I am being watched and followed.
Have you noticed any difficulties with organizing your thoughts, or has this situation significantly interfered with your ability to work and manage your daily routine?

My thoughts are completely clear and organized, so that's not an issue at all. I am still able to go to work and manage my daily routine just fine, although I do have to take different routes and be extra cautious because of the people following me.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Delusional Disorder and Schizophrenia. During the interview, the patient denied experiencing any hallucinations, disorganized thoughts, or negative symptoms, and reported that their daily functioning and ability to work remain largely intact. Since Schizophrenia typically requires the presence of other psychotic symptoms (such as hallucinations or disorganized speech) and is associated with marked functional impairment, it can be ruled out. The clinical picture of isolated, persistent persecutory beliefs with otherwise preserved functioning is highly characteristic of Delusional Disorder.
